Media and Render Core Stability Plan

purpose: Make V2 rendering more resilient, observable, cancellable, and backend-flexible while retaining the proven FFmpeg path.
evidence: Current code already uses ProcessRunner ownership, staged filter graphs, atomic destination replacement, tolerant output decoding, and real Windows FFmpeg validation.
A prior audit found real FFmpeg compatibility changes, demonstrating why tool capability detection and regression tests are necessary.
decisions: FFmpeg CLI remains the reference backend until an alternative proves equivalent or superior in controlled tests.
Every render must write to staging and atomically finalize only after validation.
Long renders must be cancellable, progress-reporting, and safe on app close.
Backend-specific optimizations must not change canonical timeline timing semantics without explicit migration approval.
tasks: Add backend capability probe with cached version/features and explicit unsupported-state messages.
Define render manifest containing source inputs, timeline duration, expected output properties, backend, options, and checksum-relevant settings.
Add post-render verification using ffprobe or equivalent: stream presence, duration tolerance, dimensions, fps, audio/subtitle expectations, non-zero file size.
Design retry policy only for safe transient failures; never silently downgrade quality or effects.
Benchmark 10, 100, and 500-scene projects; include Unicode/apostrophe/long-path Windows cases.
Plan render cache only for immutable intermediate assets with content-derived keys and explicit invalidation.
Preserve a fallback-to-reference-backend switch for V2 troubleshooting.
gate: PASS when failed renders cannot destroy a previous valid output.
PASS when cancellation and app-close behavior are deterministic.
PASS when output validation catches truncated/invalid results.
PASS when alternative backend must match reference timing and visual acceptance thresholds before default use.

purpose: Upgrade animation quality from a small render-backed subset toward a coherent keyframe/easing/effect system with preview/final parity.
evidence: Current FFmpeg native compiler explicitly supports a narrower set of capabilities across alpha, scale, rotation, and motion.
Current effect expressions use fixed short windows and intensity scaling; this is stable but limited for cinematic motion.
decisions: Separate effect identity from implementation: EffectDefinition + parameter schema + capability requirements + preview compiler + final compiler.
Add canonical keyframe curves/easing primitives instead of hardcoding every animation as bespoke FFmpeg text.
Do not advertise an effect as production-ready until both preview and final render implementations pass parity tests.
Preserve deterministic random animation with seed and lock semantics.
tasks: Define keyframe model: normalized time, value, interpolation, easing, optional velocity/overshoot parameters.
Define transforms: position, scale, rotation, opacity, crop, blur amount, shadow/glow parameters, mask/reveal progress.

Implement effect families in waves: foundational transforms; cinematic pan/zoom/drift; entrance/exit; reveal/mask; style effects; optional advanced tracking/segmentation only after mature backend support.
Define safe-zone and layout constraints so motion never unintentionally reveals empty canvas or breaks SINGLE/DOUBLE composition contracts.
Create golden scene fixtures and frame sampling tests comparing preview intent and final output.
Define user controls: duration, easing, intensity, direction, per-asset lock, copy/paste, randomize, reset.
Plan animation presets as data, not UI-hardcoded logic.
gate: PASS when every production effect has explicit preview + render support.
PASS when animation parameters serialize safely and migrate from V1 assignments.
PASS when deterministic seeds reproduce the same assignments.
PASS when motion remains within defined visual/layout constraints.

Timeline, Editing, and Feature Upgrade Plan

purpose: Mature editing behavior without discarding the current workflow or turning V2 into an uncontrolled full NLE rewrite.
evidence: Repository already contains timeline navigation, in/out, zoom/scroll, markers, magnetic controls, keyboard seek, preview seek, play selection, subtitle editing, narration recording, and validation workflows.
decisions: Keep the product focused on automatic narrative/infographic composition; add NLE-like editing only where it directly improves correction and control.
Every feature addition must map to a concrete user problem and fit ProjectState or an approved schema extension.
Manual editing must remain undoable and recoverable.
tasks: Build a compatibility matrix for all current commands/actions and mark V2 enhancements.
Standardize selection model, playhead, range, snap, markers, scene boundaries, and asset target behavior.
Plan non-destructive trim/duration editing, per-scene timing override, duplicate/move scene, copy/paste animation/style, multi-select operations, and batch validation.
Plan optional richer timeline tracks only if justified by product goals; avoid premature unrestricted multitrack editing.
Define undo/redo command granularity and transaction boundaries for batch operations.
Define validation center improvements: broken media, timing overlap, unsupported effect/backend, missing tool, provider issues, migration warnings.
gate: PASS when current workflows remain reachable with equal or fewer steps.
PASS when every mutating action participates in undo/recovery strategy.
PASS when feature additions do not silently convert the product into a generic editor with uncontrolled scope.

AI Automation, Provider, and Job Orchestration Plan

purpose: Make AI assistance more reliable and human-friendly while keeping it bounded by deterministic editing/render rules.
evidence: Current system already supports Gemini credentials in Windows Credential Manager, key slots 1-100, bounded Gemini Auto, background execution, and stale-result rejection.
Raw keys are intentionally excluded from ProjectState, logs, and status diagnostics.
decisions: AI remains an assistant that proposes/executes approved application commands; it must not bypass domain validation.
Keep Gemini as the primary provider unless a later approved plan expands providers.
Provider failures must never corrupt the project or block manual editing.
Agent text should be natural-language Indonesian for the user-facing assistant while machine contracts remain structured.
tasks: Define AI tool/command schema for scene analysis, animation assignment, validation, repair suggestions, and batch edits.
Introduce job classes with progress, cancellation, timeout, retry classification, and stale-result guards.
Design API-key pool health state: available, cooldown, quota/rate-limited, invalid, disabled; never expose secrets.
Define deterministic post-AI validation so AI cannot assign unsupported effects or invalid scene targets.
Plan conversation context boundaries and user confirmation rules for destructive/bulk actions.
Add offline/manual fallback paths for every core workflow.
gate: PASS when AI output is always validated through application/domain commands.
PASS when provider failure leaves project state unchanged or safely recoverable.
PASS when key rotation/status diagnostics reveal no secret values.
PASS when long AI work is cancellable and does not freeze UI.
